events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet Friday, increasing to 7 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 6 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM Friday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. There is potential for moderate coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

events.title: Security Council LIVE: Fragile Gulf calm tested as threats to Hormuz shipping mount
events.description: Nearly nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict. Attacks on shipping are rising, and efforts to stop a return to full-scale fighting have yet to produce a deal. The Security Council is meeting at Bahrain’s request to discuss the threat to regional and maritime security. Follow live below – and for full meetings coverage year round, go here.

events.title: COP31: Climate finance falls short as calls grow for polluters to pay
events.description: From emotional appeals for climate justice to high-stakes negotiations over billions of dollars, finance dominated discussions at COP31 on Friday. UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that even tripling adaptation funding for vulnerable countries would meet less than a third of their needs, as pressure mounted on wealthy nations and major polluters to pay their fair share.

Minor tidal overflows are possible during high tides. * WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce elevated surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor tidal overflows are possible in areas with largest surf, especially during high tide.

location.region: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Winter Storm Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. There is moderate uncertainty as to where the snow band will ultimately end up, resulting in lower confidence for snowfall amounts. Warmer temperatures filters in Sunday afternoon from east to west, transitioning snow to rain. *Low/High end values are as follows: - Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low end)/6-10" (High end). Higher elevations: up to a foot possible. - Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end). - Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible. - Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.

location.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River; East Turnagain Arm; Portage; Southern Kachemak Bay; SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula; Skilak Lake; Southern Kenai Mtns; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass

*Low/High end values are as follows:

- Anchorage/Eagle River & western Kenai Peninsula: 2-4" (Low

- Seward: 1-3" (Low end)/3-6" (High end).

- Turnagain Pass to Moose Pass: 7 to 11" possible.

- Portage: 9-11" with snowfall rates of up to 1" an hour.
weather.instruction: Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: McMullen, TX

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 13 at 8:06PM CST until November 17 at 1:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CST Friday the stage was 10.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Saturday evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early Sunday afternoon.
It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
weather.areaDesc: McMullen, TX

events.description: * WHAT...High risk of rip currents. events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 23 to 28 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 14 at 12:53AM PST until November 16 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf
conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the High Surf
Advisory, large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up
to 23 to 28 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST today. For
the High Surf Advisory, from noon today to 4 AM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

Lowest amounts near Chugiak, highest amounts South Anchorage and the Anchorage Hillside. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations). * WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM AKST Sunday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop by late this evening and continue into Sunday. Warmer air will work in aloft by late Sunday evening resulting in areas of mixed snow and freezing rain. There is still some uncertainty as to where the band of heaviest snow will develop with this system. If this band remains over the Anchorage area for an extended period of time, snow amounts could be higher.

location.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River

weather.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 14 at 5:50AM AKST until November 15 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 3 and 9 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.
Lowest amounts near Chugiak, highest amounts South Anchorage and
the Anchorage Hillside.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations).

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM AKST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop by late this evening and
continue into Sunday. Warmer air will work in aloft by late Sunday
evening resulting in areas of mixed snow and freezing rain. There
is still some uncertainty as to where the band of heaviest snow
will develop with this system. If this band remains over the
Anchorage area for an extended period of time, snow amounts could
be higher.
weather.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.
weather.areaDesc: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 30 to 35 ft this morning gradually lowering to 20 to 25 feet by this evening, then to 15 to 20 feet overnight into Sunday morning. Another round of dangerous surf conditions is expected Sunday night, with breaking waves reaching 25 to 30 ft and persisting into Monday morning. Waves and surf remain hazardous Monday, but gradually diminish through Monday evening. * WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas. Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be expected.

location.region: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 14 at 2:15AM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 30 to 35 ft this
morning gradually lowering to 20 to 25 feet by this evening,
then to 15 to 20 feet overnight into Sunday morning. Another
round of dangerous surf conditions is expected Sunday night,
with breaking waves reaching 25 to 30 ft and persisting into
Monday morning. Waves and surf remain hazardous Monday, but
gradually diminish through Monday evening.

* WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County
Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and
Brookings.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very
hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves
will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas.
Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be
expected.
weather.instruction:
Beaches and coastlines will become dangerous due to very large
and life-threatening surf conditions. Stay off of beaches, rocks,
jetties, piers, and other waterside infrastructure.
weather.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 8:54AM CST until November 17 at 1:00AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM CST Saturday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 15.0 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It
will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
weather.areaDesc: McMullen, TX

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 8 feet Friday, increasing to 8 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease to 5 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM to 4 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and potentially again Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible, especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides. Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and walkways.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to 25 to 30 feet. * WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; Central Coast of Oregon; South Washington Coast

Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme

weather.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday. * IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas... Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County. For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers, Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast. * WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden. * WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night. * IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill. Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then fall below flood stage Monday. - Flood stage is 14.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: McMullen, TX

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 7:02PM CST until November 17 at 12:24AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM CST Saturday the stage was 13.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 14.9 feet Sunday evening. It will then
fall below flood stage Monday.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
weather.areaDesc: McMullen, TX

Minor coastal flooding possible around high tide times today into Monday. * WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the Bolivar Peninsula. * WHEN...Through Monday morning. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Strong winds and elevated seas will drive wave runup further up the beach than is typically normal. There is a risk of minor coastal flooding along the low lying areas from the Bolivar Peninsula to Surfside around high tide times today into Monday.

location.region: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 14 at 9:58PM PST until November 16 at 1:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain along the south slopes of the Olympics overnight will
push the Skokomish River above flood stage Sunday morning.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Saturday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tonight to a crest of 17.1 feet late Sunday morning. It will then
fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 630 AM PST.

events.title: Beach Hazards Statement
events.description: * WHAT...High risk of rip currents. Minor coastal flooding possible around high tide times today into Monday. * WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the Bolivar Peninsula. * WHEN...Through Monday morning. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Strong winds and elevated seas will drive wave runup further up the beach than is typically normal. There is a risk of minor coastal flooding along the low lying areas from the Bolivar Peninsula to Surfside around high tide times today into Monday.

location.region: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula

weather.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 15 at 11:11AM CST until November 16 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...High risk of rip currents. Minor coastal flooding
possible around high tide times today into Monday.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong winds and elevated seas
will drive wave runup further up the beach than is typically

high tide times today into Monday.
weather.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Confidence is growing in the potential for a strong coastal storm to take a more northerly track through the Bering Sea mid-week. Depending on the final track of the system, minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts may be a possible for parts of the West Coast, with sea level rises between 3 to 7 ft possible. In addition to the coastal impact potential, periods of moderate to heavy snow and strong winds could begin as early as Tuesday night and last into Friday. The combination of winds and heavy snow could lead to reduced visibilities at times. We will continue to monitor this system closely and provide updates as additional information becomes available.

events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: A moderate, long-period north swell from 350 to 360 degrees will build across Hawaiian waters and peak later today and Monday as the period shortens to 12 seconds. The swell will produce moderate to heavy surges in north-facing harbors, especially at Kahului and Hilo Harbors. Mariners using these harbors should exercise caution when mooring or launching vessels and when entering or leaving port. The swell will diminish Tuesday.

events.description: * WHAT...Breaking waves 15 to 20 feet this morning. Conditions worsen this afternoon with breaking waves reaching 25 to 30 ft. Waves and surf remain hazardous Monday, but gradually diminish through Monday evening. * WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Monday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 8 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this evening through late Monday night. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation is expected near high tide at 1115 PM tonight and again at 1122 PM Monday night.

weather.description:

Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM this evening
to 6 AM CST Tuesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from this

or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint

Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Tuesday night.

weather.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 8 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze. * WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula. * WHEN...Until 7 AM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop by early Sunday morning and continue into early Monday morning. Warmer air will work in aloft by late Sunday night resulting in areas of mixed snow and freezing rain. There is increasing confidence in a band of steady snow falling across this region later today. If this band remains over the Kenai and Soldotna area for an extended period of time, there is a greater chance (40-50%) for higher end snowfall amounts.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations between 5 and 10 inches, with up to 12 inches through Turnagain Pass, and ice accumulations around a light glaze. * WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula, Skilak Lake, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop across the interior Kenai Peninsula by late this evening. Snow will continue through Sunday evening before warmer air begins to move over the region. Snow will likely change to rain. However, there is a chance (30-40%) for isolated pockets of freezing rain to linger in typically colder areas along the Seward Highway from Turnagain Pass to Primrose.

events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 10 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze. * WHERE...SW Kenai Peninsula and Southern Kachemak Bay. * WHEN...Until 10 AM AKST Monday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow amounts have trended higher as the steady snow looks to remain over the southern Kenai Peninsula. There is also a 30 to 40% chance for the snow to end as a brief period of light freezing rain along the Sterling Highway corridor near Ninilchik and Anchor Point.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,

rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-

weather.instruction:

producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the

Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
